correctness.rationale: For each vertex in a configuration fixed by \(U^3\), the only possibilities are permanently zero or a full \(0\to1\to2\) rotation. For the rotating set \(S\) on a \(2r\)-regular graph, the edge budget is \(\theta|S|\le\sum_{v\in S}d^+(v)\le e(S)\le r|S|\); at \(\theta=r\), equality forces \(S=V\), bichromatic edges and exactly \(r\) successor and \(r\) predecessor neighbors. The converse is checked by direct dynamics. Taking real and imaginary parts of \(Au=-ru\) with cube-root coordinates gives zero neighbors of the same color and \(r\) of each other color. Consecutive triangles in \(C_n^2\) force spatial period three and exactly six colorings precisely when \(3\mid n\). Independent `012`/`021` block concatenations give \(3\cdot2^m\) distinct threshold-one waves. Included programs were executed on 796797 literal initial states and 2795520 augmented phase assignments; finite checks are corroboration, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The half-degree contact condition is a motivated phase boundary in excitable media. It gives a general structural obstruction and a cube-root-valued spectral criterion across all finite connected even-regular graphs, then an exact all-size census on range-two rings. The contrasting \(3\cdot2^m\) threshold-one construction proves exponential-to-constant periodic-population collapse at the next contact threshold (and extinction at threshold three). This is an exact natural dynamical invariant with structural content, not a single finite computation or an arbitrary parameter slice.
